historical_403.original_environment: Web research tool; native HTTP adapter explicitly NOT_EXECUTED in that original record
historical_403.important_distinction: Do not reclassify the old web-tool 403 as a proven Node/Vercel 403. Fresh native HTTP obtained HTML; no identity changes, retries after access denial, proxies or challenge handling were used.

implementation.http_transport: Unchanged existing adapter: exact canonical HTTPS hosts/path, public IPv4 DNS checked and pinned to TLS; no redirects/retries/cookies/credentials; 8s including DNS/body; 2MiB streaming limit
implementation.structural_projection: New Cheerio acquisition adapter accepts current article/pre DOM and supported legacy DOM, validates explicit metadata, escapes only necessary text into the existing canonical musical_html shape. No musical interpretation or script execution.
implementation.review_corrections: Reject script/style nodes; omit hidden/aria-hidden descendants as the authoritative parser does; size tests reach actual bounds instead of failing on an unsupported bare pre

headless_feasibility.assessment: Conditional Node runtime capability, not implemented or proven for LouvAIO; currently unnecessary for the verified local HTML acquisition
headless_feasibility.packaging: Vercel official Puppeteer guide recommends puppeteer-core with @sparticuz/chromium-min for the standard250MB unpacked function limit. Linux binary/runtime compatibility and actual bundle must be tested, not inferred from Windows execution.
headless_feasibility.execution: Respect current repository maxDuration60, budget cold start/navigation/DOM/cleanup inside it. Official platform memory defaults and account-specific settings need confirmation; no memory/region/plan changes made.
headless_feasibility.isolation: Use an ephemeral context/profile without user cookies, tokens or session storage, close page/context/browser in finally and cap concurrency/resource budgets. A context alone is not an OS sandbox. Do not silently disable Chromium sandbox to make it launch.
headless_feasibility.ssrf: Existing Node HTTPS DNS pinning does not protect a browser automatically. All navigations, redirects, subresources, protocols, frames and DNS resolutions need enforceable egress restrictions including private IPv4/IPv6. Route interception alone is not assumed to pin DNS or isolate the network.
headless_feasibility.shared_api_risk: Adding a browser to the single existing src/app.ts function affects API bundle/cold starts/memory/concurrency; no architecture migration was made.

estimated_cost.exclusions: Traffic, browser binary downloads, platform base price, included credits, cold-start uncertainty and contention. Scenarios are not a guaranteed lower/upper bound. No bill inferred from local RSS or CPU.

android_comparison.interpretation: Different hosts/networks/stages; descriptive samples, not an A/B performance ratio. Android sample required an authorized temporary DuraSpeed setting subsequently restored; C3 made no Android changes. Backend avoids the client renderer but cloud egress and reliability remain untested.
